Continuity planning Each department must maintain a business continuity plan identifying essential services, critical suppliers, key personnel, and operational dependencies. Plans must describe how the department will operate during loss of office access, technology outage, utility disruption, or unava

Department heads must assign a primary continuity coordinator and an alternate coordinator. Continuity plans must be reviewed at least annually and whenever a material operational or technology change occurs. Service priorities Critical customer-facing services should have a documented recovery time objective of four hours or less. Important internal services should normally have a recovery time objective of 24 hours or less. Recovery point objectives must specify the maximum acceptable period of data loss for each critical system. System owners must document dependencies and recovery priorities so that infrastructure and application services are restore

em owners must document dependencies and recovery priorities so that infrastructure and application services are restored in a workable sequence. Incident activation A department head or designated continuity coordinator may request activation of the departmental continuity plan when normal operations are materially disrupted. Major incidents affecting multiple departments must be escalated to the Enterprise Incident Manager. The activation record must state the incident time, affected services, initial impact, decision owner, and communication channel. Employees must follow incident instructions and avoid publishing unapproved statements about the cause or impact of the disruption. disruption. Backup and recovery Critical business data must be backed up according to the system's approved recovery point objective. Backup copies must be protected from unauthorized alteration and access using controls appropriate to their data classification. Recovery tests for critical systems must be performed at least twice per year and documented with the achieved recovery time. A backup is not considered successfully tested until the system owner verifies that required data can be restored and used. Communication The incident communications lead maintains the official status update and ensures departments receive consistent information. Employees must use the designated emergency communication channel when corporate email or collaboration systems are unavailable. Exercise reports should capture the scenario, participants, decisions, recovery times, observed gaps, and corrective action owners. 1. Introduction
This handbook describes the working arrangements, leave entitlements, and standards of conduct
that apply to all full-time employees of Contoso Ltd. Part-time employees receive leave on a
pro-rated basis. Questions about this handbook should be sent to the Human Resources (HR)
team at hr@contoso.example.
2. Working Hours
The standard working week is 40 hours, Monday to Friday. Standard working hours are 9:00 AM to
5:30 PM, which includes an unpaid lunch break of 30 minutes. Core hours, during which
employees are expected to be available for meetings, are 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM.
Contoso operates a hybrid m

, during which
employees are expected to be available for meetings, are 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM.
Contoso operates a hybrid model. Employees are expected to work from the office on Tuesday,
Wednesday, and Thursday. Monday and Friday are remote working days unless the employee's
manager requests otherwise. Flexible start times between 8:00 AM and 10:00 AM are allowed,
provided the employee completes a full working day and is available during core hours.
Overtime must be approved in advance by the employee's line manager. Approved overtime is
compensated with time off in lieu at a rate of 1 hour for each hour worked. It is not paid in cash.
3. Attendance and Punctuality
-
Employees who will be late or absent must notify their line manager by 9:30 AM on the day, by
phone or chat message.
-
Three o

ees who will be late or absent must notify their line manager by 9:30 AM on the day, by
phone or chat message.
-
Three or more unexcused absences within a rolling 12-month period lead to a formal written
warning.
-
Repeated lateness (more than 5 late arrivals in a calendar month) will be discussed in a
one-to-one meeting with the line manager.
4. Annual Leave
Annual leave is the paid time off that employees take for vacation and personal reasons. The
yearly entitlement depends on length of service:
-
Less than 3 years: 20 working days per year
-
3 to 5 years: 23 working days per year
-
6 or more years: 25 working days per year

The leave year runs from January 1 to December 31. Employees may carry over a maximum of 5
unused annual leave days into the next year. Carried-over days must be used by March 31, or
they are forfeited. Unused leave is not paid out except when employment ends.
How to request annual leave
-
Submit the request through the HR Portal under 'Time Off'.
-
Requests for 5 or more consecutive days must be submitted at least 10 working days in
advance.
-
Requests for fewer than 5 days must be submitted at least 3 working days in advance.
-
Annual leave is approved by the employee's line manager. Managers respond within 3 working
days.

Every full-time employee receives 10 paid sick leave days per calendar year. Sick leave days do

5. Sick Leave
Every full-time employee receives 10 paid sick leave days per calendar year. Sick leave days do
not carry over to the following year. Employees must notify their line manager before 9:30 AM on
the first day of illness.
A medical certificate from a licensed doctor is required when sick leave lasts 3 or more
consecutive working days. Sick leave is separate from annual leave and cannot be deducted from
the annual leave balance. If an employee exhausts the 10 paid sick days, further absence is
unpaid unless HR approves an exception.
6. Other Types of Leave
-
Parental leave (primary caregiver): 16 weeks paid. Notify HR at least 8 weeks before the
expected start date
-
Parental leave (secondary caregiver): 6 weeks paid. Must be taken within 12 months of the
birth or adoptio

start date
-
Parental leave (secondary caregiver): 6 weeks paid. Must be taken within 12 months of the
birth or adoption
-
Bereavement leave: 5 days (immediate family) or 3 days (extended family). Immediate family
means spouse, partner, child, parent, or sibling
-
Marriage leave: 3 days paid. Taken once during employment
-
Volunteer day: 1 day per year. Must be approved by the line manager
7. Public Holidays
Contoso observes 12 paid public holidays each year: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day,
Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day,
the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, and New Year's Eve. Public holidays
are not deducted from annual leave. The company is closed on these days.

8. Code of Conduct
-
Treat colleagues, customers, and partners with respect. Harassment, discrimination, and
bullying are not tolerated and may lead to dismissal.
-
Declare any conflict of interest to your line manager and HR in writing.
-
Gifts from vendors or customers worth more than $50 must be declared to HR and may not be
accepted without approval.
-
Business casual dress is expected in the office; client-facing days may require business formal
dress.
-
Employees must not use company resources for personal commercial activity.
9. Raising Concerns
Employees who experience or witness misconduct should first speak with their line manager or
HR. Concerns may also be reported anonymously through the Ethics Hotline at 1-800-555-0142.

1. Purpose and Scope
This policy defines the rules that protect Contoso's systems, devices, and data. It applies to all
employees, contractors, and interns who access Contoso systems from any location. The IT
Security team owns this policy and can be reached at security@contoso.example or on the 24/7 IT
Security Hotline, extension 5555.
2. Password Requirements
-
Passwords must be at least 14 characters long and include a mix of upper case, lower case,
numbers, and symbols, or be a passphrase of four or more unrelated words.
-
Passwords must be changed every 180 days, and immediately if

bols, or be a passphrase of four or more unrelated words.
-
Passwords must be changed every 180 days, and immediately if compromise is suspected.
-
The last 10 passwords may not be reused.
-
Employees must never share passwords with anyone, including colleagues, managers, and IT
staff. IT staff will never ask for your password.
-
Passwords must not be written down or stored in plain-text files. Use the company-approved
password manager.
-
After 5 failed login attempts, the account is locked for 30 minutes.
3. Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
MFA is mandatory for all corporate email, VPN, cloud applications, and administrative accounts.
The approved method is the Contoso Authenticator mobile app. SMS-based codes are not
permitted. Employees with administrator privileges must also use a har

Authenticator mobile app. SMS-based codes are not
permitted. Employees with administrator privileges must also use a hardware security key. If an
MFA device is lost or stolen, the employee must report it to IT Security within 4 hours so that it can
be revoked.
4. Device Usage
-
Company laptops must have full-disk encryption enabled and must lock automatically after 5
minutes of inactivity.
-
Operating system and security updates must be installed within 7 days of release.
-
Personal devices may access company email only after enrollment in Mobile Device
Management (MDM).
-
USB storage devices and personal cloud storage services are prohibited for company data.

-
Only software from the approved software catalog may be installed. Other software requires an

required for their role. Access requests are submitted through the IT Service Portal and must be
approved by both the employee's line manager and the system owner. Access rights are reviewed
every quarter. When an employee leaves Contoso, all access is removed within 24 hours of their
last working day.

8. Security Awareness Training
All employees must complete security awareness training within 30 days of joining and every 12

Violations of this policy may result in disciplinary action, up to and including termination of
employment and, where applicable, legal action. Exceptions to this policy must be approved in
